standard starting position; variant for lesson L-FND-PIECE-BISHOP-1: quiet moves h2h3 a7a6 added so the position is not shared (checked with python-chess)

items.prompt: Slide the white bishop to the corner square h8.

claims.statement: The bishop can slide from d4 to h8.
From d4 the bishop reaches exactly 13 squares.

hints: A bishop moves along a diagonal. Which way does the line from d4 run towards the corner h8?
Count one square right and one square up at each step: e5, f6, g7, h8.
Nothing stands between d4 and h8, so the bishop can slide all the way in one move.
items.explain: d4 and h8 lie on one diagonal, and the squares between them (e5, f6, g7) are empty. A bishop slides as far as it likes along a diagonal, so it reaches the corner in one move.

items.prompt: White to move. Make one pawn move that lets the bishop on c1 out. (Several moves work; one is enough.)

claims.statement: d2d3 is a legal pawn move.
d2d4 is a legal pawn move.
b2b3 is a legal pawn move.
b2b4 is a legal pawn move.
After d2d3 the bishop on c1 can move to 5 squares.
After d2d4 the bishop on c1 can move to 5 squares.
After b2b3 the bishop on c1 can move to 2 squares.
After b2b4 the bishop on c1 can move to 2 squares.
After e2e4 the bishop on c1 still cannot move.

hints: The bishop on c1 moves along diagonals. Which two squares next to it are its first steps?
The pawns on b2 and d2 stand on those first squares.
Moving the d-pawn or the b-pawn opens one diagonal. Moving the e-pawn does not touch the c1 bishop.
items.explain: The c1 bishop is blocked by its own pawns on b2 and d2. Moving either pawn opens a diagonal for it: the d-pawn opens a long one, the b-pawn a short one. The e-pawn opens the bishop on f1, not this one.

feedback_by_move.e2e4: This frees the bishop on f1 and the queen, but the bishop on c1 is still shut in by the pawns on b2 and d2.
feedback_by_move.g2g3: This opens a diagonal for the bishop on f1, not for the bishop on c1.

items.prompt: The white bishop can take exactly one of the four black pawns. Which move does it?

claims.statement: The bishop can capture the pawn on e6.
The bishop cannot capture the pawn on c5.
The bishop cannot capture the pawn on b4.
The bishop cannot capture the pawn on d4.
The bishop's destinations are exactly these squares.

hints: A bishop moves on diagonals only. Check each pawn: is it on a diagonal of c4?
Three of the pawns stand right beside the bishop, but not on a diagonal.
Follow the diagonal c4, d5, e6.
items.explain: Only e6 is on a diagonal of c4 (c4, d5, e6, with d5 empty). The pawns on c5, b4 and d4 are straight ahead or sideways, and they stand on dark squares, which this light-squared bishop can never reach.

items.prompt: The bishop wants to reach b8, but b8 is not on a diagonal of d4. Choose a first move so that b8 can be reached with the next move.

claims.statement: b8 cannot be reached in one move from d4.
Bishop to a7 is legal.
Bishop to e5 is legal.

hints: b8 is the same colour as d4, so it can be reached; it just takes two moves. Which squares do you see from b8 along its own diagonals?
From b8 one diagonal runs down to the right: c7, d6, e5. Another touches a7.
Two squares are on both a diagonal of d4 and a diagonal of b8. Find them.
items.explain: A square of the bishop's own colour that is off its diagonals takes two moves. The first move must land on a diagonal of b8. Both a7 and e5 do, and both are reachable from d4. From either one the bishop then goes to b8.

items.prompt: Count the squares each white bishop can move to. Which bishop has more squares to choose from?

claims.statement: The bishop on b3 can move to 9 squares.
The bishop on f4 can move to 11 squares.

hints: Follow each diagonal of one bishop to the edge, one direction at a time.
The counts are close, so count carefully: a short diagonal still adds squares.
b3 has one very short diagonal; f4 has no very short one.
items.explain: The bishop on b3 reaches 9 squares and the bishop on f4 reaches 11. Neither is in a corner, so the gap is small, but the more central bishop still has more squares.

claims.statement: The bishop can capture on f6.
A black pawn stands on f6.

hints: B is the bishop, x means a capture, and the last two characters are the square.
The move ends on f6, where a black pawn stands.
The bishop on d4 slides through e5 and takes the pawn on f6.
items.explain: B names the piece, x means it captures, and f6 is the square it lands on. The bishop on d4 slides through the empty square e5 and takes the pawn on f6.

items.prompt: White to move. Tap every square the bishop can move to.

claims.statement: The bishop on f4 reaches exactly these 6 squares.

hints: Take the four diagonals from f4 one at a time.
One direction is blocked right away by a white pawn.
Another direction ends on a black pawn: you may take it, but not go past it.
items.explain: Towards the lower left the bishop's own pawn on e3 blocks the very first square. Towards the upper left it can reach e5 and capture the pawn on d6. The two right-hand diagonals are open to the edge: g5 and h6, g3 and h2.

items.prompt: After 1.e4 e5, can White's bishop on c1 move to h6? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The bishop cannot move from c1 to h6.
The bishop on c1 still cannot move.

hints: Look at the squares between c1 and h6 on the diagonal.
Which of White's own pieces stands on d2?
The e-pawn moved, not the d-pawn.
items.explain: Moving the e-pawn opens the diagonal for the f1 bishop, but the d2 pawn still blocks the bishop on c1, so it cannot reach h6.

items.prompt: White to move. Your own pawn stands on e3. Can the bishop on c1 move to g5? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The bishop cannot move from c1 to g5.
The bishop on c1 reaches only a3, b2 and d2.

hints: Trace the diagonal from c1: d2, e3, f4, g5.
What stands on e3?
A bishop cannot jump over its own pawn.
items.explain: The pawn on e3 sits on the diagonal between c1 and g5. A bishop cannot jump, and it cannot land on its own pawn, so it reaches only a3, b2 and d2.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the bishop move that gives check.

claims.statement: The bishop can move from f3 to d5.
After Bd5 the bishop attacks the black king on g8.

hints: The king sits on g8. Trace its diagonals back towards the bishop.
One diagonal from g8 runs down through f7, e6 and d5.
Which of those squares can the bishop on f3 reach?
items.explain: The diagonal g8, f7, e6, d5 crosses a diagonal of the bishop on f3 at d5. From d5 the bishop attacks g8 with nothing in between, so it is check.

items.prompt: Two black pawns stand on the long diagonal from c3. Which capture does the bishop have?

claims.statement: The bishop can capture on e5.
The bishop cannot capture on g7: the pawn on e5 is in the way.

hints: Both pawns are on the same diagonal.
The bishop meets one of them first.
A bishop cannot jump over the first pawn to reach the second.
items.explain: The pawn on e5 is the first piece on the diagonal, so it is the capture. The pawn on g7 is behind it and out of reach until e5 is gone.
